Petition under Section 166 and 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation AWARD 1.
Vide order dated 05.05.2025 passed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, present matter is remanded back to this Tribunal for hearing afresh.

2. The petitioners are seeking compensation in the wake of Detailed Accident Report (DAR) filed by police corresponding to the MACP No. 6950/16; FIR No. 489/16; PS. Mahendra Park DOD:
27.09.2025 investigation carried out in case FIR No.489/16, U/s 279/304A IPC registered at PS Mahendra Park with regard to Motor Vehicular Accident which occurred on 25.09.2016 at about 3.55 PM at GTK Road near Peer Baba Gate, Fruit Market, Azadpur Mandi, Delhi involving the vehicle bearing registration no.DL-1LT-4052 (alleged offending vehicle) being driven by respondent no. 1 Sh.Parmod in rash and negligent manner.

Detailed Accident Report (hereinafter called DAR)
filed by police, was treated as claim petition under Section 166(4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act').

3. The concise material facts of the case are that on 25.09.2016 the deceased Sh. Ravinder was working in Delhi Traffic Police and was going on motorcycle bearing no. DL-1SS-0939 and at about 3.55 PM at the gate of Fruit Mandi, Azadpur near Peer Baba Gate in the meantime a tempo bearing registration no. DL-1LT-4052 being driven in a rash and negligent manner came and hit the motorcycle of deceased which was going ahead of the tempo.
As a result of forceful impact, the deceased rider lost his control and fell down on the road.
The driver of the tempo did not stop tempo after the accident and the right wheel of the tempo ran over the traffic constable.
Thereafter the driver of the tempo stopped his vehicle after a considerable distance and he ran way from the spot.
The deceased was taken to Max Hospital where he was declared brought dead.

Case vide FIR no.
489/16 was registered at PS Mahendra Park.

It is stated that the alleged offending vehicle bearing no. DL-1LT-4052 was owned by respondent no.2 Sh. Naresh and MACP No. 6950/16; FIR No.

sentences.text: In order to prove the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle the petitioners have relied upon the testimony of eyewitness PW-2 Ct. Arvind.

He deposed that on 25.09.2016 he was posted at PS Mahendra Park and was performing duty at the gate of Fruit Mandi, Azadpur near Peer MACP No. 6950/16; FIR No. 489/16; PS. Mahendra Park DOD: 27.09.2025 Baba Gate and at about 3.55 PM, he saw a tempo bearing no. DL-1LT-4052 being driven by its driver in a zig zag manner and was overtaking the other vehicles rashly and negligently.
That suddenly the tempo driver hit against motorcycle bearing no. DL-1SS-0939 being driven by a traffic constable, going ahead of the tempo.
As a result of forceful impact, the traffic constable lost his control and fell down on the road.
He immediately rushed towards the motorcyclist and help him.
The tempo driver stopped his vehicle after a considerable distance after looking behind at the injured and then he fled away from the spot.
He took the injured to Max Hospital in a TSR, where he was declared brought dead.
IO/SI Devi Lal came at the spot and recorded his statement.
Site plan was prepared at his instance and the offending vehicle was also seized.
Thereafter he reached at PS Mahendra Park where the tempo driver was already present and he identified the injured.
Driver of the tempo was arrested.
He categorically deposed that the accident took place due to sole negligence on the part of tempo driver who hit the motorcyclist from behind while driving his vehicle in a zig zag manner.
The testimony of PW-2 has gone unchallanged on the part of driver and owner.
In the cross- examination on behalf of insurance company, he deposed that the deceased gave signal to the tempo driver in order to stop him but he did not stop the same.
He also denied the suggestion that the deceased in order to stop the tempo, all of sudden stopped his motorcycle in front of the tempo while driving at a fast speed.
He further denied the suggestion that the accident took place due to negligence of deceased himself.
MACP No. 6950/16; FIR No. 489/16; PS. Mahendra Park DOD: 27.09.2025 10.

Arvind has categorically deposed regarding negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle i.e. respondent no.1.
The respondents could not impeach his testimony through litmus test of cross- examination and said witnesses is found to have successfully withstood the test of cross-examination.
There is no reason as to why he would depose falsely against respondent no.1.

Moreover, the respondents have not led any evidence to rebut the testimony of aforesaid witness on the aspect of accident in question being caused due to rash and negligent driving of tempo bearing no.DL-1LT-4052.
Respondent no.1/driver of aforesaid tempo, was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident had taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of tempo bearing no.DL-1LT-4052 by him.

11. Thus, issue no. 1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.

14. Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 enjoins upon the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.

15. The intent and objective of the Beneficial Legislation is to grant equitable compensation to the vulnerable victims of road accidents and dynamic law has evolved towards grant of just and fair quantum of awards MACP No. 6950/16; FIR No. 489/16; PS. Mahendra Park DOD: 27.09.2025 and has brought consistency and uniformity towards the desired goal.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in "Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation" (2009) 6 SCC 121, which was affirmed by a bench of three Hon'ble Judges in Reshma Kumari & Ors. Vs. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, held as under:
"16.

sentences.text: "Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.
It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit.
17. Assessment of compensation though involving certain hypothetical considerations, should nevertheless be objective.
Justice and justness emanate from equality in treatment, consistency and thoroughness in adjudication, and fairness and uniformity in the decision making process and the decisions.
While it may not be possible to have mathematical precision or identical awards, in assessing compensation, same or similar facts should lead to awards in the same range.

When the factors/inputs are the same, and the formula/legal principles are the same,
consistency and uniformity, and not divergence and freakiness, should be the result of adjudication to arrive at just compensation..."

16. These guiding principles for assessment of "just and reasonable compensation" have been torch bearer in injury cases also as laid down by Hon'ble Delhi High Court, in III (2007), ACC 676 titled as Oriental MACP No. 6950/16; FIR No. 489/16; PS. Mahendra Park DOD: 27.09.2025 Insurance Co,.
Ltd., Vs. Vijay Kumar Mittal & Ors, wherein it has been held:-

sentences.text: The possession of one's own body is the first and most valuable all human rights and while awarding compensation for bodily injuries this primary element is to be kept in mind.
Bodily injury is to be treated and varies on account of gravity of bodily injury.

Though it is impossible to equate money with human suffering, agony and personal deprivation, the Court and Tribunal should make an honest and serious attempt to award damages so far as money can compensate the loss.
Regard must be given to the gravity and degree of deprivation as well as the degree of awareness of the deprivation.
Damages awarded in personal injury cases must be substantial and not token damages....."

11. The general principle which should govern the assessment of damages in persons injury cases is that the Court should award to injured persons such a sum as will put him in the same position as he would have been in the same position as he would have been in if he had not sustained injuries".
17.

The Hon'ble Apex Court, in further development of the legal position for grant of reasonable and fair compensation, has pronounced guiding parameters that "the compensation should be just and is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly or a pittance".
Reliance is placed on 2012 (8) SLT 676 titled K. Suresh Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.

It is a well expected norm that money can not substitute a life lost but an effort has to be made for grant of just compensation having uniformity of approach.
There has to be a balance between the two extremes, that is, a windfall and the pittance, a bonanza and the modicum....."
18. Accordingly, the entitlement of petitioner to just compensation is being assessed in the background of well settled parameters and guidelines as discussed herein-above.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Detailed Accident Report (hereinafter called DAR)
filed by police, was treated as claim petition under Section 166(4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act').
As a result of forceful impact, the deceased rider lost his control and fell down on the road.
The driver of the tempo did not stop tempo after the accident and the right wheel of the tempo ran over the traffic constable.
Thereafter the driver of the tempo stopped his vehicle after a considerable distance and he ran way from the spot.
The deceased was taken to Max Hospital where he was declared brought dead.
The respondents could not impeach his testimony through litmus test of cross- examination and said witnesses is found to have successfully withstood the test of cross-examination.
Moreover, the respondents have not led any evidence to rebut the testimony of aforesaid witness on the aspect of accident in question being caused due to rash and negligent driving of tempo bearing no.DL-1LT-4052.
Respondent no.1/driver of aforesaid tempo, was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident had taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of tempo bearing no.DL-1LT-4052 by him.
11. Furthermore, the respondents no.1 Sh.Parmod(accused in State case) has been charge sheeted for offences punishable U/s 279/304A IPC by the investigating agency after arriving at the conclusion on the basis of investigation carried out by it, that the accident in question had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing no.DL-1LT-4052 by him.

Azadpur Mandi, Delhi due to rash and negligent driving of the tempo bearing registration no.DL-1LT-4052 by respondent no. 1 Sh.Parmod.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Hon'ble Apex Court in "Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation" (2009) 6 SCC 121, which was affirmed by a bench of three Hon'ble Judges in Reshma Kumari & Ors. Vs. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, held as under:
"16.
The Hon'ble Apex Court, in further development of the legal position for grant of reasonable and fair compensation, has pronounced guiding parameters that "the compensation should be just and is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly or a pittance".
Reliance is placed on 2012 (8) SLT 676 titled K. Suresh Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
LOSS OF DEPENDENCY 19.
(Reliance is placed on judgment passed in case titled "Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Shashi Sharma & Ors.", 2016 ACJ 2723(SC))
22.
Here it will be suffice to mention that in the present case, it has not been shown if the ex-gratia amount received by the claimants had been under any Rules of service and would be of continuous assistance, as had been the case in Shashi Sharma(supra) as per the Rules of 2006 considered therein.
Even otherwise, insurance company has also failed to lead any evidence in this regard.
In an overall analysis and with reference to the decision passed in case titled "Sabastiani Lakra & Ors. Vs.
National Insurance Company Ltd. & Ors., 2019 ACJ 34(SC), this Tribunal is clearly of the view that the decision in Shashi Sharma (supra) would not apply to the facts of the present case and thus,
there would be no deduction of ex-gratia amount.
The deceased is stated to be aged about 28 years at the time of accident.
Hence the deceased was around 28 years of age at the time of accident.
LOSS OF CONSORTIUM 34.
Respondent no. 3/insurance company has not claimed exemption on account of any statutory breach as envisaged u/s.149(2) MV Act.
They have not adduced any evidence in absence of any statutory defence.
